subject: Procurement: split-award strategy for CDN/WAF renewals
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement: split-award strategy for CDN/WAF renewals

Team —

We’ve got three major renewals coming up across our CDN/WAF layer (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai) between Jan–Mar. Instead of a single re-bid, I’m proposing a split-award approach: keep Cloudflare for global edge and WAF, award Fastly for low-latency API egress in NA/EU, and keep Akamai as regional backup for APAC failover. The goals are: reduce unit cost by 10–20%, keep SLA coverage for latency-sensitive endpoints, and avoid a single-vendor blast radius.

Attached is a first-pass cost comparison and a short runbook (mop-split-award-draft.docx). Key asks:
- Marissa: validate traffic segmentation feasibility with infra (routes, zones)
- Laura: confirm procurement timelines and whether split PO/awards are ok for finance
- Jordan: any legal flags for multi-vendor SLAs / termination windows?

If we agree, I’ll open SOWs with each vendor and request mutual action plans (MAPs). Looking to finalize strategy by 11/29 so we can hit vendor negotiation cycles in Dec.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: cost-comparison-2026.xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: split-award strategy for CDN/WAF renewals

Ben —

Quick read through the sheet. A couple of operational notes:
- Segmenting by path/hostname is straightforward for the API gateway (we already route /api/* to dedicated edge pools). That will let us direct low-latency traffic to Fastly.
- Session affinity for streaming endpoints is trickier across providers — we’ll need sticky routing or session proxying for those endpoints. That adds ~1–2ms and some infra dev work.
- I’ll sync with infra on capacity for maintaining two active CDNs and estimate run-rate ops cost.

Timelines: Finance will accept split POs but we need consolidated invoicing option for accounting simplicity. Laura, can you confirm if consolidated billing is a hard requirement or just preferred?

Happy to jump on a quick call with vendor reps next week.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@cloudflare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Dubois <sophie.dubois@fastly.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: split-award strategy for CDN/WAF renewals

Ben / team —

Appreciate the heads-up and the comparison. Cloudflare can offer a blended discount with a 12-month commitment and an optional 30% traffic credit for burst months. We can also scope a narrower WAF policy set for API endpoints to reduce rule execution cost.

Notes:
- Draft amendment and MAP available if you can share expected qps and peak 95th percentile for the API endpoints (we only need 90-day sample).
- We can add a failover origin directive for the Fastly pool, but that requires standard health-checks and TTL adjustments.
- SLA: we’re willing to add a 10ms latency credit to the SLA for API edge if we’re primary for those routes (requires product approval).

Attaching a short pricing summary in-line (attachment: cloudflare-proposal-summary.pdf). Happy to do a 30-minute technical call with Marissa and infra.

Jordan Miller
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Cloudflare
jordan.miller@cloudflare.com
(attachment: cloudflare-proposal-summary.pdf)

Subject: Re: Procurement: split-award strategy for CDN/WAF renewals

Ben / team —

Legal review (high level):
- Multi-vendor approach is fine. We need to ensure:
  1) Clear termination triggers for each vendor (we should avoid overlapping cure periods to prevent simultaneous failover storms).
  2) Data handling clauses aligned across vendors — please confirm whether any vendor will see unredacted PII; if so, we need identical DPA terms.
  3) SLA credits must be cumulative and easy to claim — avoid ones that require separate ticketing paths per vendor.

Requested deliverables before we sign: vendor MAPs, proposed amendment drafts, and the consolidated financial summary (one spreadsheet is fine). I’ve attached a short redline checklist (attachment: contract-redlines-request.pdf).

If we want to move fast, schedule a vendor MAP review on 11/29. Otherwise we risk not finishing commercial terms before the holidays.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: contract-redlines-request.pdf)
